title: Efficient Scaledown: the four capabilities and what each one solves
purpose: Efficient Scaledown capabilities. The coupling problem; Remote Shuffle Manager; Shuffle Migration; Decision Layer; AQE Shuffle Write; Measured effect and platform constraints.
accessibleSummary: Efficient Scaledown capabilities. The coupling problem; Remote Shuffle Manager; Shuffle Migration; Decision Layer; AQE Shuffle Write; Measured effect and platform constraints.
longDescription: Efficient Scaledown capabilities. The coupling problem; Remote Shuffle Manager; Shuffle Migration; Decision Layer; AQE Shuffle Write; Measured effect and platform constraints.

nodes.label: Shuffle output is glued to local disk
nodes.summary: Shuffle data on executor-local disk blocks safe scale-down and risks stage recompute.
nodes.detail: Shuffle data on executor-local disk blocks safe scale-down and risks stage recompute.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle data on executor-local disk blocks safe scale-down and risks stage recompute.

evidence.note: Shuffle data written to each executor's local disk prevents release until downstream stages finish reading.
Losing an executor holding shuffle data raises FetchFailedException and forces stage re-execution.

inputs: A shuffle-heavy job with autoscaling enabled
processing: Retain executors holding unread shuffle output
outputs: Idle but billed executors, or costly recomputes
drill.example: An executor sits idle for minutes purely because a later stage has not yet fetched its blocks.
failureModes: Aggressive scale-down triggers stage recomputes that cost more than the compute saved.

nodes.label: Spark's own partial answer
nodes.summary: Spark's graceful decommissioning and pluggable shuffle IO are the foundation Fabric builds on.
nodes.detail: Spark's graceful decommissioning and pluggable shuffle IO are the foundation Fabric builds on.
nodes.whyItMatters: Spark's graceful decommissioning and pluggable shuffle IO are the foundation Fabric builds on.

evidence.note: Graceful decommissioning migrates shuffle blocks to a peer or fallback storage before the executor exits.
spark.shuffle.sort.io.plugin.class is the documented extension point for redirecting shuffle data to remote storage.

drill.example: An executor being decommissioned copies its blocks to a peer before terminating.
failureModes: Both settings default to false, so the protection is absent unless deliberately enabled.

nodes.label: Remote Shuffle Manager
nodes.summary: Remote Shuffle Manager writes shuffle data to Blob Storage instead of local disk.
nodes.detail: Remote Shuffle Manager writes shuffle data to Blob Storage instead of local disk.
nodes.whyItMatters: Remote Shuffle Manager writes shuffle data to Blob Storage instead of local disk.

evidence.note: Efficient Scaledown routes shuffle output to Azure Blob Storage, decoupling shuffle data from executor lifetime.
A Remote Shuffle Manager reads and writes shuffle data to remote Blob Storage.

processing: Write shuffle blocks to remote Blob Storage
outputs: Shuffle data independent of executor lifetime
drill.example: An executor finishing its tasks can be released immediately because its shuffle output lives remotely.
failureModes: Remote writes add network latency, which is why routing every shuffle remotely is not optimal.

nodes.label: Shuffle Migration
nodes.summary: Shuffle Migration moves locally held blocks to a peer before an executor exits.
nodes.detail: Shuffle Migration moves locally held blocks to a peer before an executor exits.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle Migration moves locally held blocks to a peer before an executor exits.

evidence.note: Efficient Scaledown includes shuffle migration among its four cooperating parts.

processing: Migrate blocks to a peer before exit
drill.example: Blocks kept local by the Decision Layer are moved rather than lost when the executor scales down.
failureModes: Migration takes time, so very aggressive scale-down can still outpace it.

nodes.label: Decision Layer
nodes.summary: The Decision Layer routes large shuffles remotely and keeps small ones local.
nodes.detail: The Decision Layer routes large shuffles remotely and keeps small ones local.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Decision Layer routes large shuffles remotely and keeps small ones local.

evidence.note: A per-stage decision layer routing only large shuffles to remote storage delivers up to 57% faster runtime than routing all shuffles remotely.

processing: Route large shuffles remote, small shuffles local
drill.example: A small broadcast-scale exchange stays on local disk while a multi-terabyte shuffle goes remote.
failureModes: Routing decisions are per stage, so a mixed stage cannot be split further.

nodes.label: AQE Shuffle Write
nodes.summary: AQE Shuffle Write shapes the blocks handed to remote shuffle storage.
nodes.detail: AQE Shuffle Write shapes the blocks handed to remote shuffle storage.
nodes.whyItMatters: AQE Shuffle Write shapes the blocks handed to remote shuffle storage.

evidence.note: Efficient Scaledown's four parts work together, including adaptive shuffle write behaviour.
AQE coalesces post-shuffle partitions toward the advisory target size.

processing: Shape partitioning during the write itself
drill.example: Remote storage receives a modest number of well-sized blocks rather than thousands of tiny ones.
failureModes: Without write-side shaping, remote shuffle storage receives many small blocks and pays more overhead.

nodes.label: What Microsoft measured
nodes.summary: Microsoft reports a 54% compute reduction and up to 57% faster runtime from per-stage routing.
nodes.detail: Microsoft reports a 54% compute reduction and up to 57% faster runtime from per-stage routing.
nodes.whyItMatters: Microsoft reports a 54% compute reduction and up to 57% faster runtime from per-stage routing.

evidence.note: In Microsoft's TPC-DS benchmark on Spark 4.1 total compute dropped from 14,952 to 6,880 VM-minutes with Efficient Scaledown enabled.

processing: Run with and without Efficient Scaledown
drill.example: The benchmark ran all queries in one session with a three-minute pause between them.
controls: Benchmark conditions materially affect the result
failureModes: Quoting the headline number for a workload with little shuffle overstates the benefit.

nodes.label: Constraints that gate adoption
nodes.summary: Efficient Scaledown requires the native engine and explicit configuration to enable.
nodes.detail: Efficient Scaledown requires the native engine and explicit configuration to enable.
nodes.whyItMatters: Efficient Scaledown requires the native engine and explicit configuration to enable.

evidence.note: Efficient Scaledown requires the Native Execution Engine and is available from Fabric Spark Runtime 3.5 and later.
Enabling it requires explicit Spark configuration properties rather than being on by default.

outputs: A go or no-go adoption decision
drill.example: A regulated estate must confirm its storage and networking constraints before planning on the savings.
failureModes: Assuming it is on by default means the savings never materialize.

edges.label: Spark addresses part of it upstream
Pluggable shuffle IO enables remote storage
Decommission framework is tuned by Fabric
Routing decides which shuffles go remote
Combined capabilities produce the measured saving
Gains are conditional on the prerequisites
